A native of [[Chesterton, Indiana]], McGary declared for the [[NBA draft]] after completing his sophomore season for the [[2013–14 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team]]. He was drafted 21st overall by the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] in the [[2014 NBA draft]]. At the time of his [[National Letter of Intent]] signing with [[Michigan Wolverines basketball]], [[ESPN.com]] and [[Scout.com]] ranked McGary as the number two player in the United States high school class of 2012, while [[Rivals.com]] ranked him as the number three prospect. He was not only the consensus top [[Power forward (basketball)|power forward]] recruit in the nation,{{cite web|url=http://www.michigandaily.com/sports/touted-hoops-recruit-mcgary-commits-michigan|title=Touted hoops recruit Mitch McGary commits to Michigan|access-date=November 18, 2011|date=November 3, 2011|publisher=[[Michigan Daily]]|author=Estes, Ben}} but also the top [[Glossary of basketball terms#B|big man]] according to most sources at the time.{{cite web|url=http://content.usatoday.com/communities/campusrivalry/post/2011/11/top-big-man-recruit-mitch-mcgary-commits-to-michigan/1|title=Nation's No. 2 basketball recruit Mitch McGary commits to Michigan|access-date=December 31, 2011|date=November 3, 2011|work=[[USA Today]]}} After his signing, however, McGary fell down in the rankings as his underdeveloped offensive skills became apparent. At Michigan, McGary became the [[sixth man]] as well as the leading [[blocked shot|shot blocker]] and [[rebound (basketball)|rebounder]] for the [[2012–13 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team]]. During the season, he was twice named Big Ten Freshman of the Week. He became the regular starter during the [[2013 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament]]{{cite web|url=http://www.michigandaily.com/sports/mcgary-robinson-will-return-2013-14-season|title=McGary, Robinson will return for 2013-14 season|access-date=April 18, 2013|date=April 18, 2013|work=[[Michigan Daily]]|author=Thomas, Colleen}} and earned South All-Regional Team and NCAA All-Tournament Team recognition as he helped the team reach the [[2013 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship Game|championship game]]. He led all Big Ten freshmen in rebounding. ==Early life== [[File:20110110 Mitch McGary at Hoop Hall Classic.jpg|thumb|left|McGary at [[Brewster Academy|Brewster]], 2011]] Mitch McGary was born on June 6, 1992,{{cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120221152546/http://www.usabasketball.com/mens/hoopsummit/roster.html|archive-date=February 21, 2012|url-status=dead|url=http://www.usabasketball.com/mens/hoopsummit/roster.html|title=Nike Hoop Summit - USA & World Team Rosters|access-date=March 14, 2012|publisher=[[USA Basketball]]}} and grew up in the [[Chesterton, Indiana]], area. He played in [[YMCA]] and [[Amateur Athletic Union]] (AAU) basketball leagues as a youth, and his father, Tim, who had never played organized sports, coached him until fourth grade.{{cite web|url=http://www.dukehoopblog.com/2011/10/12/through-the-eyes-of-a-father-mitch-mcgary/|title=Through the Eyes of a Father: Mitch McGary|access-date=November 18, 2011|date=October 12, 2011|work=Duke Hoop Blog|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111114225338/http://www.dukehoopblog.com/2011/10/12/through-the-eyes-of-a-father-mitch-mcgary/|archive-date=November 14, 2011|url-status=dead}} McGary's mother is named Valerie.{{cite web|url=http://www.michigandaily.com/sports/mitch-mcgary-you-dont-know-through-eyes-his-parents|title=The Mitch McGary you don't know, through the eyes of his parents|access-date=March 31, 2013|date=November 8, 2012|work=Michigan Daily|author=Wasserman, Daniel}} When McGary was younger, his father thought his athletic future was in [[baseball]]. McGary played on the 2007–08 [[Chesterton High School]] [[junior varsity team]] as a freshman, while eventual three-time [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan Wolverines]] [[captain (sports)|captain]] [[Zack Novak]] was a senior on the [[varsity team]]. That year he also was a {{convert|6|ft|6|in|m|2|adj=on}}, {{convert|190|lbs|kg|0|adj=on}} freshman [[tight end]] on the [[high school football]] team, but his father made him quit football as he continued to grow.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/collegebasketballnation/post/_/id/81287/mcgary-offers-a-new-dimension-for-michigan|title=McGary offers new dimension for Michigan|access-date=March 24, 2013|date=March 23, 2013|publisher=[[ESPN]]|author=Rothstein, Michael}} His local Indiana SPY Players AAU basketball team included future Michigan teammates [[Max Bielfeldt]] and [[Glenn Robinson III]], son of [[Glenn Robinson]]. McGary joined the varsity basketball team the following season and played two years. McGary is afflicted with [[attention deficit hyperactivity disorder]]. He eventually transferred to [[Brewster Academy]], a prep school in [[Wolfeboro, New Hampshire]], to repeat his junior year because his parents thought the discipline would be good for him. Before transferring to Brewster, McGary was the tallest kid in his school and in the basketball conference that he played in.
